target: Ils ont un chien et un chat.
english: They have a dog and a cat.
grammar: 'Être pressé' = to be in a hurry. The adjective agrees: pressé/pressée.

target: Ils sont très fatigués après le voyage.
english: They are very tired after the journey.
Which movie do you want to see?

target: Comment on va à la gare ?
english: How do we get to the station?

grammar: 'Qu'est-ce qui' = What (as subject). Use when 'what' is doing the action: Qu'est-ce qui fait ce bruit ? (What's making that noise?)
'Qu'est-ce que c'est ?' is a fixed expression meaning 'What is this/that?' Very useful for learners.
'Comment' = How/What. 'Comment tu t'appelles ?' is informal. Formal: 'Comment vous appelez-vous ?'
'Une bière' is feminine. Most drinks ending in -ère are feminine: une bière, une rivière.

target: Il y a du vent aujourd'hui.
grammar: 'Du/de la/des' for partial quantities: 'Je mange du pain' = I eat some bread (not all bread).

target: Est-ce que tu viens ce soir ?
grammar: 'Être' (to be): je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont.

target: Est-ce que tu aimes le fromage ?
grammar: 'Aimer' + definite article for general likes: 'tu aimes le fromage' (cheese in general). Without article = specific cheese.
'Qu'est-ce que' = What (as object of verb). Use for 'what' questions: Qu'est-ce que tu veux ? (What do you want?)
'Où' (where) with accent distinguishes it from 'ou' (or) without accent. The accent matters in writing.
'Pourquoi' = Why. Can be followed by subject+verb directly or by 'est-ce que': Pourquoi est-ce que tu ris ?
'Quand' = When. Use with 'est-ce que' or inversion: Quand pars-tu ? / Quand est-ce que tu pars ?
The inverted question form 'parlez-vous' is more formal than 'est-ce que vous parlez'. Both are correct.
'Lequel/laquelle' = which one. Agrees in gender and number: lequel, laquelle, lesquels, lesquelles.
In casual French, you can put the question word at the end: Tu viens d'où ? Tu fais quoi ? C'est qui ?

target: Est-ce que vous acceptez les cartes ?

grammar: 'À qui' = to whom / whose: 'À qui est ce livre ?' = Whose book is this?

target: Quand est-ce que tu es libre ?

grammar: 'La' is the feminine singular definite article. Use 'la' before feminine nouns starting with a consonant: la maison, la table, la rue.
'Les' is the plural definite article for both masculine and feminine nouns: les garçons, les filles, les maisons.
'De la' is the feminine partitive article meaning 'some'. Use for feminine uncountable nouns: de la salade, de la soupe, de la viande.
'Bon' (m.) → 'bonne' (f.) = good. Most adjectives add -e for feminine: petit → petite, grand → grande.
Possessives: ton/ta/tes (your, informal). Before feminine nouns starting with a vowel, use 'mon/ton/son' instead of 'ma/ta/sa': mon amie.
'De' replaces partitives after negation, but NOT after 'ne...que' (only): 'Je ne bois que du café'.

target: Je ne mange jamais de viande.
grammar: 'Ne...jamais de' = never any. Same rule: un/une/du/de la become 'de' in negative: Je ne bois jamais de café.
'Long' (m.) → 'longue' (f.) = long. Irregular feminine form. Some adjectives change more than just adding -e.
'Chaud' (m.) → 'chaude' (f.) = hot. 'Froid' → 'froide' = cold. Regular feminine form: just add -e.
'Gros' (m.) → 'grosse' (f.) = big/fat. Multiple adjectives: size before noun + color after: un gros chien noir.
'Leur' is the indirect object pronoun for 'them': 'ce restaurant leur plaît' = this restaurant pleases them.
'Il me faut' = I need (literally: it is necessary to me). Reverse construction: il me faut, il te faut, il lui faut, il nous faut.
'Suffire' (to be enough) is impersonal like falloir: 'il suffit de' = it's enough to.

target: Parlez plus lentement, s'il vous plaît.
grammar: 'C'est gentil' = that's kind. A common way to thank someone for their thoughtfulness.
'Quel/quelle' (which/what) agrees with the noun: quel livre (m.), quelle heure (f.), quels jours (m.pl.).

target: Où est-ce que tu as grandi ?

grammar: 'Depuis quand' = since when. 'Depuis combien de temps' = for how long. Both use present tense in French.

target: Quel est le mot de passe du wifi ?
Où est-ce que tu as trouvé ça ?

grammar: 'Des' is the plural indefinite article: des frites = some fries. It's required in French where English often uses nothing.
'Nouveau' has special forms: nouveau (m. before consonant), nouvel (m. before vowel), nouvelle (f.), nouveaux (m. pl.), nouvelles (f. pl.).

target: Je mange un sandwich au jambon.

grammar: Possessive adjectives agree with the noun, not the owner: mon père (m.), ma mère (f.), mes parents (pl.).
'Son/sa/ses' = his/her/its. The form matches the following noun's gender, not the possessor: son mari (her husband, m.).

target: Il y a trop de bruit.
Le bureau du directeur est grand.
grammar: 'Du' = de + le (contraction). 'Des' = de + les. These contractions are mandatory: le livre du professeur, les jouets des enfants.

target: La porte de l'école est fermée.
grammar: Countries have articles too: la France, le Japon, les États-Unis. Use 'en' for feminine, 'au' for masculine.
'Au' = à + le (contraction). 'Aux' = à + les. Mandatory: je vais au cinéma, je parle aux enfants. No contraction with la or l'.

target: Il n'y a plus de lait.
grammar: 'Ne...plus de' = no more. Like 'ne...pas de', the article disappears after negative + de: Il n'y a plus de pain.
'Premier' (m.) → 'première' (f.) = first. Ordinal numbers go before the noun and agree: le premier, la première.
Nationality adjectives ending in -ien change to -ienne in feminine: italien → italienne, canadien → canadienne.

target: Je suis en train de manger.
grammar: 'Être en train de + infinitive' = to be in the process of doing. Use to emphasize an ongoing action: Je suis en train de travailler.

english: How do you get to work?
grammar: 'Aller à' = to go to. 'Au' = à+le: 'vous allez au marché' = you go to the market.

english: What are you doing this weekend?
Who are you going out with?
grammar: 'De quoi' = about what/of what. Used with verbs that take 'de': 'De quoi parlez-vous ?'

target: Enchanté de faire votre connaissance enfin.
english: Delighted to finally make your acquaintance.
Since when have you lived here?
grammar: 'Depuis quand' = Since when. 'Depuis combien de temps' = For how long. Both use present tense in French (not past).

english: How do you spell your name?

target: Où est-ce que tu as garé la voiture ?
english: Where did you park the car?
Who is coming to the party?
When are we seeing each other?

target: Le chat dort sur le canapé.
english: The cat sleeps on the couch.
grammar: 'Le' is the masculine singular definite article. Use 'le' before masculine nouns starting with a consonant: le chat, le livre, le train.

target: Le livre est sur la table.
english: The book is on the table.
grammar: 'Livre' is masculine (le livre), 'table' is feminine (la table). You must memorize the gender of each noun.

target: Il met du sucre dans son thé.
english: He puts sugar in his tea.

target: Une salade verte et un steak.
english: A green salad and a steak.

target: Le musée est fermé le lundi.
english: The museum is closed on Mondays.
He eats a lot of vegetables.
grammar: After expressions of quantity (beaucoup de, peu de, trop de, assez de), always use 'de' without article: beaucoup de pain (not du pain).

english: The cup of tea is full.

english: How much time do you need?
grammar: Three question forms: intonation ('Tu viens?'), 'est-ce que', or inversion ('Viens-tu?').

english: Do you have any time left?
grammar: 'Rester' can be impersonal: 'il me reste du temps' = I have time left. Reversed construction.

target: Zéro, un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq.
english: Zero, one, two, three, four, five.

target: Une femme attend à l'arrêt de bus.

grammar: 'Une' is the feminine singular indefinite article (a/an). Use before feminine nouns: une femme, une table, une fleur.

target: J'achète du fromage et de la confiture.
english: I buy some cheese and some jam.
grammar: 'Du fromage' (some cheese) and 'de la confiture' (some jam) – partitive articles show an unspecified amount.

target: Les jouets des enfants sont par terre.
english: The children's toys are on the floor.

target: Il faut une heure pour y aller.
english: It takes an hour to get there.

target: Viens ici, j'ai besoin de ton aide maintenant.

target: Quelqu'un a laissé la fenêtre ouverte toute la nuit.

target: Nulle part ailleurs on ne trouve un tel fromage.

grammar: 'Excusez-moi' (formal) vs 'excuse-moi' (informal). Used to get attention or apologize.

target: D'abord il faut comprendre les règles du jeu.
english: First you need to understand the rules of the game.

grammar: Adjectives ending in -eux change to -euse in feminine: sérieux → sérieuse, heureux → heureuse, curieux → curieuse.
'Le soleil' – celestial bodies always take the definite article: le soleil, la lune, les étoiles.
'Plein/pleine' agrees with the noun: 'la lune est pleine' (feminine). Masculine: 'le verre est plein'.
Adjectives agree in gender and number. 'Sympa' is invariable informally, but standard form: sympathique/sympathiques.
'Beau' has special forms: beau (m. before consonant), bel (m. before vowel), belle (f.), beaux (m. pl.), belles (f. pl.).
'Être' (to be): je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont.
In French, abstract nouns need an article: 'la liberté', 'l'amour'. English often drops it.
Nationality adjectives are lowercase in French: français(e), anglais(e), espagnol(e). They agree in gender and number.
After 'c'est', use the indefinite article: 'C'est un ami' (He's a friend), not *'C'est ami'.

target: Un sac à dos bleu marine.

grammar: 'Sportif' (m.) → 'sportive' (f.). Adjectives ending in -if change to -ive in feminine: actif → active, positif → positive.
'Frais' (m.) → 'fraîche' (f.) = fresh/cool. Irregular feminine form with accent: frais/fraîche.
When two BANGS adjectives are before a noun, the order is generally: size + other quality: un joli petit village, un grand beau jardin.
'Manquer à' is reversed like 'plaire': 'ma famille me manque' = my family is missing to me. The thing missed is the subject.
'Manquer' agrees with its subject: 'mes amis me manquent' (plural subject = plural verb).

target: Il nous faut plus de chaises.

grammar: 'Déranger' = to bother/disturb. The thing bothering is the subject: Le bruit me dérange = The noise bothers me.
'Un' is the masculine singular indefinite article (a/an). Use before masculine nouns: un homme, un livre, un café.
'Des' is the plural indefinite article (some). Use before plural nouns: des livres, des amis, des fleurs. In negative: des → de.
In negative sentences, un/une/des/du/de la all become 'de' (or d'): Je n'ai pas de voiture. Il n'y a pas de lait.
Some adjectives go BEFORE the noun (BANGS: Beauty, Age, Number, Goodness, Size): petit, grand, beau, bon, jeune, vieux, nouveau.
Color adjectives go AFTER the noun and agree: une robe bleue, un pantalon bleu, des chaussures bleues.
'Blanc' (m.) → 'blanche' (f.) = white. Some adjectives have irregular feminine forms.

target: Elle prend du jus de pomme.

grammar: 'Leur' (their, singular) and 'leurs' (their, plural): leur fils, leurs enfants. 'Leur' doesn't change for gender.
Adjective agreement in plural: add -s (or -es for feminine): noir → noirs (m. pl.), noire → noires (f. pl.).

target: Le jardin de mon voisin est joli.
grammar: Possession uses 'de': le livre de Marie (Marie's book), la voiture de mon père (my father's car). No apostrophe-s in French.
Some color adjectives are invariable (never change form): marron, orange, rose (when used for specific shades). Exception: rose does agree.

target: J'ai acheté une tarte aux pommes.

grammar: 'Il me reste' = I have left (literally: there remains to me). Reverse construction like falloir: il me reste, il te reste.
'Faire plaisir à' = to make happy/to please. Reverse: the thing causing pleasure is the subject.
'Intéresser' = to interest. The topic is the subject: Ce livre m'intéresse = This book interests me (= I'm interested in this book).

target: Il a annulé la réservation à l'hôtel.
Tu es parti sans dire au revoir.
grammar: With être verbs, the past participle agrees with the subject: tu (masculine) to parti.

target: La clé est dans mon sac.
english: The key is in my bag.
grammar: 'La clé' is feminine. In French, you must memorize the gender of each noun – there are few reliable rules.

target: Notre maison est au bord de la mer.
english: Our house is by the sea.
grammar: 'Notre' (our, singular) and 'nos' (our, plural): notre maison, nos enfants. Same form for masculine and feminine singular.

english: I have a kilo of tomatoes.

target: Il me reste un peu de lait.
english: I have a little milk left.

target: Il est parti très tôt ce matin.
english: He left very early this morning.
grammar: 'Partir' uses 'être': il est parti. The past participle agrees: elle est partie, ils sont partis.

target: Tu as essayé le nouveau restaurant ?
english: Did you try the new restaurant?

target: Elles sont retournées à l'hôtel après le dîner.
english: They returned to the hotel after dinner.

target: Attention, la route est glissante après la pluie.
english: Careful, the road is slippery after the rain.

target: Nous avons trouvé un bon restaurant près de l'hôtel.
english: We found a good restaurant near the hotel.

grammar: With plaire, use indirect object pronouns: me (to me), te (to you), lui (to him/her), nous, vous, leur. The thing liked is subject.
When the subject (thing liked) is plural, plaire becomes 'plaisent': Ces chaussures me plaisent = I like these shoes.
'Ça me plaît' is the most common way to say 'I like it' in casual French. More natural than 'j'aime ça'.
'Tu me manques' literally = You are missing to me = I miss you. The person missed is the subject, the person feeling the lack is the indirect object.
'Être' (to be): je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont.
'Plaisent' is plural because 'ces fleurs' is plural. Plaire agrees with its subject (the thing liked).
'Manquer à' is reversed from English: 'Mon pays me manque' = My country is missing to me = I miss my country. The thing missed is subject.
'Manquer à quelqu'un' reverses English word order. 'La France te manque' = France misses to you = You miss France.
'Déplaire à' is the opposite of 'plaire à': Ça me déplaît = I don't like that. Same reverse construction.
'Chauve' (bald) doesn't change in feminine – it already ends in -e: il est chauve, elle est chauve.
'Timide' is the same in masculine and feminine: il est timide, elle est timide.
'Bavard' (m.) → 'bavarde' (f.) = talkative/chatty. Personality adjectives follow the noun: un homme bavard, une femme bavarde.
'Cet' is used before masculine nouns starting with a vowel or silent 'h': cet homme, cet arbre, cet hôtel.
'Être' (to be): je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont.
'Bon/bonne' goes BEFORE the noun and is irregular: bon/bonne (not *bone). 'Un bon repas'.
Adjectives ending in -eux form feminine with -euse: heureux/heureuse, curieux/curieuse.
Compound adjectives with colors don't agree: 'des yeux bleu foncé' (not *bleus foncés).
'Être' (to be): je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont.
'Bonjour' is used from morning to evening. Use 'bonsoir' after around 6 pm. 'Comment allez-vous ?' is formal.
'Au' = à+le, 'aux' = à+les. Mandatory contractions. 'À la' and 'à l'' don't contract.
'Plaire à' has a reverse construction: the thing liked is the subject. 'Ce film me plaît' = This movie pleases me (= I like this movie).
'Plaire à' works backwards from English: 'cette musique te plaît ?' = does this music please you? Subject and object are swapped.
Three question forms: intonation ('Tu viens?'), 'est-ce que', or inversion ('Viens-tu?').
The imparfait describes ongoing, habitual, or background past actions. Formed from the 'nous' present stem + -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient.
'Vous' here is formal singular. In formal French, always use 'vous' with strangers and superiors.

target: Ma grand-mère a les cheveux blancs.
grammar: 'Blanc/blanche' has an irregular feminine form. The pronunciation changes from [blɑ̃] to [blɑ̃ʃ].

target: Il est patient avec les enfants.

grammar: 'À tout à l'heure' = see you later (today). 'À plus tard' = see you later (less specific). 'À bientôt' = see you soon.
Weather uses 'il fait' + adjective: il fait beau (nice), il fait chaud (hot), il fait froid (cold), il fait mauvais (bad).

target: Exactement, tu as compris le problème principal.
english: Exactly, you understood the main problem.

target: Il est blond aux yeux bleus.
english: He is blond with blue eyes.
grammar: 'Aux yeux bleus' = with blue eyes. 'Aux' is the contraction of 'à les'. Used for physical descriptions.

target: Elle est brune aux yeux verts.
english: She is brunette with green eyes.
grammar: 'Brun/brune' changes form for gender. 'Vert/verte' also changes. The final consonant is pronounced in feminine.

english: My son is three years old.

target: Tu as bu assez d'eau aujourd'hui ?
english: Did you drink enough water today?

target: Elles ont dit au revoir à leurs amis.

grammar: 'Au' = à+le, 'aux' = à+les. Mandatory contractions. 'À la' and 'à l'' don't contract.

target: Elles ont pris le petit déjeuner à l'hôtel.
english: They had breakfast at the hotel.

target: Ils ont pris le train de huit heures.
english: They took the eight o'clock train.

target: Ça me fait plaisir de te voir.
english: It makes me happy to see you.

target: Il me semble que c'est vrai.
english: It seems to me that it's true.
grammar: 'Il me semble que' = It seems to me that. 'Sembler' uses the same reverse pattern: il me semble, il te semble.

english: I can't wait to see you again.
grammar: 'Il me tarde de' = I can't wait to (literary). Same as 'j'ai hâte de' but with reverse construction.

english: It's not serious. / No big deal.

target: Personne ne connaissait la réponse à cette question.
english: Nobody knew the answer to this question.
I would like a glass of water.
grammar: 'Je voudrais' (conditional of vouloir) is the polite way to say 'I would like'. More polite than 'je veux' (I want).

target: Tout est prêt pour le départ de demain matin.
english: Everything is ready for tomorrow morning's departure.

target: La chambre est au deuxième étage.
english: The room is on the second floor.
grammar: French floors: rez-de-chaussée (ground floor), premier étage (1st floor = US 2nd floor), deuxième étage (2nd = US 3rd).

target: Ils ont ouvert un nouveau restaurant en ville.
english: They opened a new restaurant in town.

target: J'ai mis trois heures pour arriver.
english: It took me three hours to arrive.
grammar: Mettre can express duration: j'ai mis + time means it took me + time.

target: Ils ont ouvert leur magasin il y à deux ans.
english: They opened their store two years ago.

target: Ça te dit d'aller au cinéma ?
english: Do you feel like going to the movies?
grammar: 'Ça te dit de...' = Do you feel like...? Literally 'Does that say to you to...' Another reverse construction.

target: Dépêche-toi, le train part dans dix minutes!
english: Hurry up, the train leaves in ten minutes!

target: Ensuite nous irons acheter des provisions au marché.
english: Then we'll go buy groceries at the market.
grammar: 'Pas du tout' = not at all. Stronger negation than a simple 'non'.

target: Doucement, le bébé dort dans la chambre.
english: Quietly, the baby is sleeping in the room.

target: Tellement de monde est venu à la fête hier.
english: So many people came to the party yesterday.
grammar: 'Quand même' = still / even so / all the same. Very common in conversation to express surprise or insistence.

target: Nous dînons en famille le dimanche.
english: We have dinner as a family on Sundays.

target: Tu as bu tout le café ce matin ?
english: Did you drink all the coffee this morning?
grammar: Three question forms: intonation ('Tu viens?'), 'est-ce que', or inversion ('Viens-tu?').

target: Aussitôt dit, aussitôt fait, le problème est réglé.
english: No sooner said than done, the problem is solved.
grammar: Weather verbs use 'il' (impersonal): il pleut (raining), il neige (snowing), il y a du vent (windy), il y a du brouillard (foggy).

target: Lentement mais sûrement il apprend à jouer du piano.
english: Slowly but surely he's learning to play the piano.

target: Je voudrais réserver une table pour deux.
english: I would like to reserve a table for two.

target: Assez parlé, passons maintenant aux choses sérieuses.
english: Enough talk, let's move on to serious matters now.

target: Je voudrais une chambre avec vue sur la mer.
english: I would like a room with a sea view.

target: Elle a ouvert les rideaux pour voir le jardin enneigé.
english: She opened the curtains to see the snowy garden.

grammar: 'S'il vous plaît' (formal/plural) vs 's'il te plaît' (informal). Literally 'if it pleases you'. Essential polite expression.
'S'il te plaît' (informal) vs 's'il vous plaît' (formal). Literally: 'if it pleases you'.
'D'accord' = OK/agreed. Shortened to 'd'ac' in very informal speech.
'En fait' = actually/in fact. A very common discourse marker in spoken French.
'Nouveau/nouvelle' has a special form before masculine vowels: 'un nouvel ami' (not *un nouveau ami).
'Jaloux' (m.) → 'jalouse' (f.) = jealous. Adjectives ending in -oux change to -ouse in feminine: doux → douce (exception).
'Mignon' (m.) → 'mignonne' (f.) = cute. Adjectives ending in -on double the 'n' in feminine: bon → bonne, mignon → mignonne.
'Je vous en prie' is the most formal way to say 'you're welcome'. More casual: 'de rien' or 'pas de quoi'.
'Pardon' = sorry (quick apology). 'Je suis désolé(e)' = I'm sorry (deeper apology). 'Excusez-moi' = excuse me.
'Bien sûr' = of course. Can be intensified: 'mais bien sûr !' (but of course!).

Adjectives ending in -if form feminine with -ive: actif/active, sportif/sportive.

'Être' (to be): je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont.

'Je m'appelle...' = My name is... Literally 'I call myself'. This is a reflexive verb: s'appeler.

target: Vingt et un, trente, quarante, cinquante.
grammar: Numbers 21-69 follow a pattern: vingt et un (21), trente-deux (32). After 70, French uses base-20: soixante-dix (70), quatre-vingts (80).
'N'importe' = it doesn't matter. 'N'importe quoi' = anything/whatever/nonsense.
Directions: à gauche (left), à droite (right), tout droit (straight ahead), en face de (across from), à côté de (next to).
'Chapeau !' = hats off/well done. An informal way to express admiration.

target: Il se rase tous les matins.

grammar: 'Ne...jamais' in passé composé: 'je n'ai jamais vu' (I never saw). 'Jamais' replaces 'pas'.
Most descriptive adjectives go AFTER the noun in French, but some common ones (BANGS) go before. Predicate adjectives go after être.
Adjectives agree in gender: petit/petite, mince stays the same (ends in -e already). Two adjectives joined by 'et'.

target: Elle a les cheveux longs et bouclés.
grammar: 'Long/longue' has an irregular feminine. The 'g' becomes 'gu' to keep the hard [g] sound.
'Jeune' doesn't change in feminine (already ends in -e). Most adjectives ending in -e are invariable for gender.
'Âgé/âgée' – the circumflex accent on 'â' is part of the spelling, not just pronunciation.
BANGS adjectives go BEFORE the noun: Beauty, Age, Number, Goodness, Size. 'Une belle femme', not *'une femme belle'.
Compound color adjectives are invariable (no agreement): bleu foncé, vert clair, bleu marine. They stay the same regardless of gender/number.
'Ça y est' = That's done / All set. Used when something is finished or accomplished.

target: La réunion est à quelle heure ?
On se retrouve à quelle heure ?
Tu as cuisiné quelque chose de bon ?
Nous avons signé le contrat hier.
grammar: Passé composé expresses completed actions in the past.

target: Nous avons commandé des pizzas pour le dîner.
J'ai fini de manger à midi.
grammar: The past participle of finir is fini. Regular -ir verbs drop -r: finir to fini.

target: Nous avons peint la chambre en bleu.
Le chat est gris et blanc.
english: The cat is grey and white.

target: Elle est fière de son travail.
english: She is proud of her work.
grammar: 'Fier' (m.) → 'fière' (f.) = proud. The accent changes: fier/fière. 'Fier de' = proud of.

english: Maybe we should change our approach.

target: Ensemble nous pouvons accomplir de grandes choses.
english: Together we can accomplish great things.
Sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, one hundred.
grammar: 70 = soixante-dix (60+10), 80 = quatre-vingts (4×20), 90 = quatre-vingt-dix (4×20+10). Unique to French counting.

target: Comment est-ce qu'on prononce ce mot ?
english: How do you pronounce this word?
On the other hand, it's expensive.

target: À mon avis, c'est trop cher.
english: In my opinion, it's too expensive.
grammar: 'À mon avis' = in my opinion. Useful for expressing opinions: À mon avis, à ton avis, à votre avis.

english: I need to send this email.

target: Je me lève à sept heures.
english: I get up at seven o'clock.
grammar: Reflexive verbs use reflexive pronouns: je me lève, tu te lèves, il se lève, nous nous levons. The pronoun matches the subject.

target: Tu as regardé le film hier ?
english: Did you watch the movie yesterday?
grammar: Passé composé for 'regarder': j'ai regardé, tu as regardé. Regular -er verbs form past participle with -é.

target: Il a marché jusqu'à la garé.
english: He walked to the train station.

target: J'ai rangé ma chambre ce matin.
english: I tidied my room this morning.

target: Tu as acheté un billet aller-retour ?
english: Did you buy a round-trip ticket?
grammar: In questions, the structure stays the same: tu as + past participle. Intonation rises.

target: Nous avons passé deux semaines en Espagne.
english: We spent two weeks in Spain.

target: Il est entré dans la pièce sans frapper.
english: He entered the room without knocking.
grammar: Entrer uses être: il est entre. DR MRS VANDERTRAMP verbs all use être.

target: Ils ont économisé de l'argent pour les vacances.
english: They saved money for the vacation.
I threw away the old newspapers.

target: Il a téléphone à son frère en Allemagne.
english: He called his brother in Germany.

target: Il est sorti acheter du pain.
english: He went out to buy bread.
grammar: Sortir uses être when intransitive: il est sorti.

target: J'ai arrosé les plantes ce matin.
english: I watered the plants this morning.

target: Bravo, tu as réussi ton examen avec brio!
english: Well done, you passed your exam brilliantly!
grammar: 'Bravo' is borrowed from Italian and is invariable. 'Avec brio' = brilliantly, also from Italian.

target: Toujours elle arrive en retard au cours de français.
english: She always arrives late to French class.
grammar: 'Arriver' uses 'être' in passé composé: 'je suis arrivé(e)'. 'En retard' = late. Regular -er in present.

target: Justement, c'est ce que je voulais dire.
english: Precisely, that's what I wanted to say.

target: Rien n'est impossible quand on travaille ensemble.
english: Nothing is impossible when we work together.

target: Je prends un aller-retour pour Lyon.
english: I'll take a round-trip ticket to Lyon.

target: Le train part de quel quai ?
english: Which platform does the train leave from?

target: J'ai mangé au restaurant hier soir.
english: I ate at the restaurant last night.
grammar: 'Au restaurant' uses 'au' (à + le). Time markers like 'hier soir' confirm passé composé.

target: J'ai préparé le dîner pour toute la famille.
english: I prepared dinner for the whole family.

target: Elle a compté l'argent dans son portefeuille.
english: She counted the money in her wallet.
grammar: In passé composé with avoir, the past participle of -er verbs ends in -e.

target: Tu as lu le journal ce matin ?
english: Did you read the newspaper this morning?

target: Il est revenu de son voyagé hier.
english: He came back from his trip yesterday.
grammar: Revenir uses être: il est revenu. Past participle agrees with subject.

target: J'ai réservé deux places pour le concert.
english: I reserved two seats for the concert.

target: Nous avons célèbre son anniversaire au restaurant.
english: We celebrated her birthday at the restaurant.

target: Elles ont aidé leurs parents à préparer le repas.
english: They helped their parents prepare the meal.

target: Nous sommes restés à l'hôtel ce jour-là.
english: We stayed at the hotel that day.
grammar: Rester uses être. Masculine plural subject: restes.

target: Nous avons fermé le magasin à vingt heures.
english: We closed the store at eight PM.

target: Tu as noté le numéro de téléphone ?
english: Did you write down the phone number?

target: Elle a ouvert un livre et a commencé à lire.
english: She opened a book and started reading.

target: Écoute, je dois te dire quelque chose d'important.
english: Listen, I need to tell you something important.
grammar: 'Écoute' is the informal imperative (tu form) of 'écouter'. Used as an interjection to get attention.

target: Regarde le beau coucher de soleil sur la mer.
english: Look at the beautiful sunset over the sea.
grammar: 'Regarde' is the tu-form imperative. 'Regardez' for vous-form. Both can be used to draw attention.

target: Cependant il reste encore beaucoup de travail.
english: However, there's still a lot of work left.

target: Chacun doit apporter sa contribution au projet.
english: Everyone must bring their contribution to the project.

target: J'ai une réservation au nom de Dupont.
english: I have a reservation under the name Dupont.

target: Debout, il est déjà sept heures du matin!
english: Get up, it's already seven in the morning!

target: Il a cherché ses clés pendant une heure.
english: He looked for his keys for an hour.

target: Nous avons attendu le bus pendant vingt minutes.
english: We waited for the bus for twenty minutes.

target: J'ai attendu le train pendant trente minutes.
english: I waited for the train for thirty minutes.
grammar: Attendre uses avoir: j'ai attendu. The -u ending is typical for -re verbs.

target: Elle cuisinait toujours un bon repas le dimanche.
english: She always cooked a good meal on Sundays.
grammar: Weather in the past uses imparfait: il pleuvait, il faisait beau.

target: Il est descendu du bus au bon arrêt.
english: He got off the bus at the right stop.
grammar: Descendre uses être when there is no direct object: il est descendu.

target: Tu savais que le magasin fermait a dix-huit heures ?
english: Did you know the store closed at six PM?

target: Elle ouvrait sa boutique à neuf heures.
english: She used to open her shop at nine o'clock.

target: Nous discutions pendant des heures au téléphone.
english: We used to talk for hours on the phone.
grammar: The imparfait of 'être' (j'étais) is one of the most useful forms. 'J'étais fatigué' = I was tired. States in the past = imparfait.

target: Tu savais déjà parler anglais à dix ans ?
english: Did you already know how to speak English at ten?
grammar: 'Déjà' + imparfait describes a state that was already true: 'tu savais déjà' = you already knew.

target: Je préparais toujours le thé à cinq heures de l'après-midi.
english: I always used to make tea at five in the afternoon.

target: Tu connaissais déjà la réponse quand le professeur a pose la question ?
english: Did you already know the answer when the teacher asked the question?
grammar: 'Toujours' or 'souvent' in past context → imparfait (habitual). 'Un jour' or 'soudain' → passé composé (specific event).
Days of the week: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche. No capitals. 'Le lundi' = on Mondays (habitual).
